title: Molecular Characterization of Human Adenoviruses Before and After a Severe HAdV‐7 Military Outbreak in Finland in 2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand factors contributing to a severe HAdV‐7 outbreak in Finnish military garrisons in 2024 by reviewing adenovirus types circulating before the outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a retrospective surveillance of adenovirus‐positive respiratory samples collected from 2013 to 2023 and enhanced surveillance from 2024 to 2025 in Finnish garrisons. A total of 497 samples were typed during the initial period, and 1692 samples were typed during the outbreak period.
analysis.methods: Adenovirus types were identified using type‐specific PCR assays targeting specific strains, and whole‐genome sequencing was performed on 11 selected samples to analyze the outbreak-associated HAdV‐7d strain.
analysis.main_results: During 2013–2023, HAdV‐4 was the most common type (n = 446; 89.7%), followed by HAdV‐3 (n = 25; 5%), HAdV‐21 (n = 11; 2.2%), HAdV‐7 (n = 6; 1.2%), and HAdV‐11 (n = 1; 0.2%). Between February 2024 and June 2025, HAdV‐4 was detected in 1133 samples (67%), HAdV‐7 in 440 samples (26%), with co-detection of HAdV‐4 and ‐7 in 70 samples (4.1%) and HAdV‐14 in 1 sample (0.1%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that HAdV‐7d, the virus associated with the 2024 outbreak, was already circulating in Finnish garrisons in 2023, suggesting that limited prior circulation may have contributed to the outbreak's severity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of active surveillance in tracking adenovirus circulation and inform the development of targeted preventative measures to mitigate future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on surveillance data and does not include direct causal evidence, but the results are supported by whole‐genome sequencing and epidemiological investigation, providing moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the molecular characterization of human adenoviruses in Finnish military garrisons before and after a severe HAdV‐7 outbreak in 2024. Retrospective surveillance from 2013–2023 revealed HAdV‐4 as the most common type, followed by HAdV‐3, HAdV‐21, HAdV‐7, and HAdV‐11. Enhanced surveillance from 2024–2025 showed a shift in prevalence, with HAdV‐7 becoming dominant. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed that the outbreak strain, HAdV‐7d, had been circulating since 2023. The authors suggest that the outbreak's severity may be due to limited prior circulation of HAdV‐7 in Finland. The study underscores the value of active surveillance in understanding adenovirus dynamics and implementing effective prevention strategies.

title: A comprehensive analysis of molecular epidemiology and clinical characteristics of human adenovirus among hospitalized children with pneumonia in Tianjin, China, 2022–2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are a major pathogen associated with acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children worldwide. However, the epidemiological and genotypic characteristics of HAdV among pediatric inpatients with ARIs have not been fully elucidated in Tianjin.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Respiratory specimens were collected from children hospitalized with ARIs between September 2022 and August 2025. The main clinical diagnoses included pneumonia, bronchitis, tonsillopharyngitis, and upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs). HAdV-3, HAdV-7 and HAdV-1 were the dominant circulating genotypes among hospitalized children with ARIs in Tianjin from 2022 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Targeted next-generation sequencing was used for initial screening and typing of HAdV. Randomly selected positive samples were further analyzed by conventional PCR amplification targeting the hexon gene, followed by phylogenetic analysis using reference sequences from GenBank. A total of 19,523 specimens were tested, yielding an overall HAdV detection rate of 8.7% (1,704/19,523).
analysis.main_results: HAdV was detected year-round with marked seasonal variation ( P < 0.001) and a clear peak in winter (13.4%, 573/4,285). The detection rate was significantly higher in males than in females ( P = 0.002). Significant differences were observed across age groups ( P < 0.001), with the highest detection rate in the 3–6 years age group (11.9%, 551/4,611).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Genotype–phenotype association analysis revealed that HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 were predominant in pneumonia cases, whereas HAdV-3 and HAdV-1 were common in tonsillopharyngitis and URTIs. Importantly, children infected with HAdV-7 were more likely to develop severe pneumonia ( P < 0.001).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support region-specific surveillance and targeted interventions, and provide epidemiological evidence to inform the rational design and formulation of multivalent vaccines against pediatric HAdV.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Age-specific, seasonal, and inter-annual shifts in genotype distribution were observed, with HAdV-B replacing HAdV-C as the dominant species after August 2023. The supplied evidence does not report on the limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a comprehensive analysis of the molecular epidemiology and clinical characteristics of human adenovirus (HAdV) among hospitalized children with pneumonia in Tianjin, China, from 2022 to 2025. It aimed to examine the epidemiological features, genotype distribution, and clinical associations of HAdV infection. Respiratory specimens were collected from children with acute respiratory infections (ARIs), and targeted next-generation sequencing was used for initial screening and typing, followed by conventional PCR amplification targeting the hexon gene and phylogenetic analysis. The overall HAdV detection rate was 8.7%, with a higher rate observed in males and the 3–6 years age group. HAdV-3 and HAdV-7 were predominant in pneumonia cases, while HAdV-3 and HAdV-1 were common in tonsillopharyngitis and URTIs. Children infected with HAdV-7 were more likely to develop severe pneumonia. The findings highlight the need for region-specific surveillance and targeted interventions, and provide epidemiological evidence for the development of multivalent vaccines against pediatric HAdV. The study observed shifts in genotype distribution over time, with HAdV-B replacing HAdV-C after August 2023. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of detailed limitations in the supplied text.

title: Establishment of a CD46 and desmoglein-2 expressing mouse model for human adenovirus type 55 vaccine evaluation

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of a physiologically relevant small-animal model for evaluating HAdV-55 vaccine candidates, given the emerging nature of HAdV-55 as a respiratory pathogen with no licensed vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed a transgenic mouse model co-expressing human CD46 and desmoglein-2 (DSG-2) to evaluate vaccine efficacy, using mice from multiple centres.
analysis.methods: A bicistronic expression system was constructed to enable simultaneous expression of CD46 and DSG-2, and the model was functionally validated in vitro. Mice were vaccinated with an inactivated HAdV-55 (iHAdV-55) vaccine formulated with alum and challenged with HAdV-55.
analysis.main_results: The transgenic mice showed dose-dependent weight loss, robust viral replication in lung tissues, and characteristic histopathological changes following viral challenge. Vaccination induced strong HAdV-55-specific IgG and neutralizing antibody responses, and vaccinated mice exhibited reduced weight loss and accelerated recovery compared to controls.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study established the CD46/DSG-2 transgenic mouse as a physiologically relevant model for HAdV-55 infection and demonstrated that iHAdV-55 vaccination confers robust humoral immunity and protective efficacy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This model provides a critical tool for the development and preclinical evaluation of adenovirus-targeted vaccines and therapeutics, addressing the need for better models to evaluate HAdV-55 vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a transgenic mouse model, which may not fully recapitulate all aspects of human infection, and the need for further validation in larger animal models.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a transgenic mouse model expressing human CD46 and DSG-2 to evaluate HAdV-55 vaccine efficacy. The model demonstrated robust viral replication and immune responses, confirming its utility for vaccine development.

title: Prolonged survival after systemic immune reactivation by aglatimagene besadenovec plus valacyclovir in immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory non-small cell lung cancer.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer who progress on immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) face limited options and poor survival. analysis.study_design_and_population: In this open-label, phase 2a clinical trial, 76 patients were enrolled (intention-to-treat population) and 73 received at least one dose of aglatimagene besadenovec (safety population); 46 patients who received two intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec injections, completed protocol-defined valacyclovir exposure, and underwent a 12-week imaging comprised the evaluable (per-protocol) population.
analysis.methods: Endpoints included clinical and immunological outcomes. Exploratory biomarkers demonstrated systemic immune reactivation, including cytotoxic T-cell expansion and regression of uninjected lesions, with stronger signals in non-squamous histology.
analysis.main_results: In the 73 patients included in the safety analysis (including patients who did not receive a second injection due to apparent pseudoprogression), median OS was 14.3 months. In the evaluable (per-protocol) population of 46 patients who completed protocol-defined treatment and week-12 imaging, median OS was 24.5 months (95% CI 16.0 to 33.8). Among the 41 evaluable patients in cohort 2, 15 (37%) were alive at ≥24 months and 5 (12%) at ≥40 months.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In this single-arm phase 2a study, aglatimagene besadenovec plus valacyclovir with ongoing ICI was associated with systemic immune remodeling and encouraging survival.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 2a clinical trial evaluated aglatimagene besadenovec, a replication-defective adenoviral vector, in combination with valacyclovir for patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory non-small cell lung cancer. title: Identification and functional characterization of ASCC2 as a diagnostic biomarker and immune regulatory hub in Kawasaki disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis in children, yet its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify downregulated candidate diagnostic biomarkers and subsequently investigate the potential functional relevance of a prioritized candidate gene in KD.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Bulk transcriptomic data from GSE73461 were used for biomarker discovery and model development, while GSE68004 was used for independent external validation. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE168732 were further analyzed to investigate the cellular and regulatory characteristics of the identified genes.
analysis.methods: Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine learning algorithms, CellChat, and scTenifold-based perturbation analysis were performed. Functional investigation of the prioritized candidate ASCC2 was performed in TNF-α-stimulated HUVECs using siRNA-mediated knockdown.
analysis.main_results: Three consistently downregulated genes (EPB42, RUNDC3A, and ASCC2) were identified as candidate diagnostic biomarkers for KD. The three-gene model achieved an AUC of 0.903 in the discovery cohort and 0.948 in the independent GSE68004 cohort. In clinically relevant febrile controls, the model showed moderate discrimination between KD and human adenovirus infection (AUC = 0.830) and between KD and Group A streptococcal infection (AUC = 0.769).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings identify EPB42, RUNDC3A, and ASCC2 as a reproducible molecular signature associated with KD. These findings support the diagnostic potential of the three-gene panel while providing preliminary mechanistic insights into ASCC2 in KD.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the diagnostic potential of the three-gene panel as an adjunctive molecular marker for KD, rather than a standalone diagnostic tool. This could inform future studies on KD diagnostics and immune regulation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on transcriptomic data and in vitro functional analyses, which may not fully capture in vivo complexity. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of external validation cohorts and the focus on a single gene for mechanistic investigation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify downregulated candidate diagnostic biomarkers for Kawasaki disease (KD) and investigate the functional relevance of a prioritized gene, ASCC2. Using bulk transcriptomic data from GSE73461 and GSE68004, the researchers identified three genes—EPB42, RUNDC3A, and ASCC2—as a potential molecular signature for KD. The three-gene model showed strong discrimination between KD and healthy controls, with moderate performance against febrile infections like human adenovirus and Group A streptococcal infections. ASCC2 was further investigated through single-cell and in silico analyses, revealing its role in NK-cell cytotoxicity and cell-cycle regulation. Functional experiments in TNF-α-stimulated HUVECs showed that ASCC2 knockdown reduced cell viability and induced G0/G1-phase arrest. These findings suggest the three-gene panel could serve as an adjunctive diagnostic marker for KD, with preliminary insights into ASCC2's role in immune regulation. However, the study's reliance on transcriptomic and in vitro data limits its generalizability and the strength of its conclusions.

title: From ward to wastewater: optimising near-source surveillance for microbial targets in hospitals

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hospitals generate wastewater enriched with human-derived microbes, making them strong sites for focused, near-source surveillance of pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We compared in-sewer 24-h composite and passive sampling at two hospital discharge locations and influent sampling at a municipal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP).
analysis.methods: We also evaluated three extraction workflows to determine how sampling and extraction methods influence detection sensitivity across faecal indicators (HF183, crAssphage) and clinically relevant pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, human adenovirus, Campylobacter jejuni).
analysis.main_results: Across 14 consecutive days, HF183 and crAssphage quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) cycle threshold (Ct) signals were stronger in hospital wastewater than at the WWTP, consistent with greater human faecal input at the near-source sites.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: crAssphage and human adenovirus were detected with comparable Ct values in passive and liquid samples, whereas the bacterial targets HF183 and C. jejuni were detected less sensitively by passive sampling, particularly at one hospital site.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This pattern was consistent with site-specific wastewater composition and flow dynamics affecting membrane retention.
